newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Good weather boosts Ukraine winter wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: Good weather boosts Ukraine winter wheat crop.

text.p: Good weather has paved the way for Ukraine to harvest around 20 million tonnes of winter wheat this year, up from last year's 13.1 million tonnes, the chief of Ukraine's Weather Forecasting Centre said on Friday.
"Rains in the last part of May somewhat improved the previous situation" of dryness in many parts of Ukraine in early spring, Mykola Kulbida told Reuters.
"The total winter crop is expected at nearly 20 million tonnes," he said.
Kulbida said yields of 3.1 tonnes per hectare were expected compared to 2.24 tonnes last year. Ukraine also sowed small amounts of rye and barley as part of the winter grain crop.
He said some areas in the southern and central sections were dry, while moisture conditions in the rest of the former breadbasket of the Soviet Union were good to excellent.
Spring weather throughout Ukraine has been cooler and wetter than last year, when drought in early spring was blamed for pushing the total grain harvest down to 25.4 million tonnes.
Kulbida did not provide weather forecasts for the spring crop, whose sowing is complete at 13.51 million hectares, up from 13.12 million planted last year.
Private farmers' sown area to early spring grains was flat at 4.647 million hectares.

Agriculture Minister Mykhailo Zubets, also deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, has forecast the total grain crop at 35 million tonnes and predicted Ukraine's grain exports would be double this year to six million tonnes.
Ukraine exports some of its grain to Russia and other former Soviet republics, as well as to Eastern and Central Europe.
He has also said the maize crop would be "significantly better" than last year's 1.8 million tonnes. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 244-9150
